question: According to its own data, on a three-figure number of occasions over the past years, while conducting aeroplane and drone surveillance operations, the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex) sent out distress signals to all nearby ships within the operational area rather than just following the usual procedure of just informing the competent search and rescue authorities. 1.
On how many occasions have distress signals been sent out to all nearby vessels by Frontex aircraft, and how does this number break down by year for 2022, 2023 and 2024?
In which operational areas did this occur in which years, and which Frontex service (e.g. joint operations, multipurpose aerial surveillance, Eurosur) was responsible?
On which occasions were the distress signals sent out by aeroplane pilots and on which occasions by drone operators?
answer: As the question regarding ‘Distress signals sent out by Frontex aircraft’ falls entirely under the responsibility of the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex), the Commission has asked the Agency to provide the details requested by the Honourable Member. The Agency’s reply will be sent by the Commission to the Honourable Member as soon as possible. See annexes: Annex 1, Annex 2, Annex 3.
